source.note: companion file on the MetroPT-2 record; renamed locally to make its role explicit; 'train' is the depositors' naming, NOT an ML split -- failure windows verified present 2026-09-20

paper: Veloso, Ribeiro, Gama, Pereira (2022), Scientific Data 9:764, DOI 10.1038/s41597-022-01877-3
columns: same 21-col schema as MetroPT2.csv (gpsLong/gpsLat order swapped); see metropt2_manifest.json sensor semantics

failure_events.disposition: severe malfunction, removed from service (paper F1 section; blown pipe photo in maintenance report; data: 03:00-05:00 gap = stopped, LPS off 06:25)
failure_events.provenance: Veloso 2022 Table 2 (published version); W2-2026-09-21 empirical adjudication of attribution conflict: LPS 4h continuous + oil temp ceiling 97.9C + outage gap = severe blown client pipe. NOTE arXiv:2207.05466v3 and arXiv:2508.05388 swap F1/F2 components ( dryer<->clients ) -- published version is physically correct; see runs/label_check/W2_label_crossvalidation.md section 4

failure_events.disposition: recovered autonomously, train continued in operation (pilot valve returned to normal pattern after 15:00)
failure_events.provenance: Veloso 2022 Table 2 (published version); no LPS trigger all day (empirical); attribution conflict note as event 1

failure_events.disposition: severe compressor damage, removed from service
failure_events.provenance: Veloso 2022 Table 2 (published) AND arXiv:2207.05466v3 Table 1 -- both print end 2022-06-02 06:18; empirically CONFIRMED: first LPS trigger 06:18:33 (paper 'end' = operator-observable failure moment to the minute). W1's earlier 'end = file end 15:49' hypothesis REFUTED: file end is the export boundary, recording continued 9.5h past the failure end
failure_events.end_note: anchor = 06:18 per both published sources + LPS trigger; data gap after 15:49 is export cutoff, not removal time

cross_validation_2026_09_21.labels_verified: all three events: type/component/start/end cross-checked against data signatures (see label_check/W2_label_crossvalidation.md)

physical_ceilings.note: both ceilings recur on train B for the same failure classes -- sensor/physical limit, not coincidences; question-bank rules must avoid absolute oil-temp thresholds

cross_validation_2026_09_21.healthy_band_oil_temp: mean 61-64C, daily max 71-76C (train A); train B (MetroPT2.csv) differs: mean 54-57C, max 62-65C -- per-vehicle calibration required
cross_validation_2026_09_21.gvbeta_lead: github.com/gvbeta/MetroPT does NOT exist (GitHub API 404); paper's code-availability section names no repository -- lead closed

verification_2026_09_20.open_item: dataset_train carries exactly 5/6 of MetroPT2's samples on shared days (72001 vs ~86400x1Hz) -- characterize the thinning pattern in W2 (second-of-minute distribution; possibly deliberate 5-in-6 thinning or parked-period exclusion); does not affect window construction

design_role: TRAIN A stream for the industrial case: 3 documented failures x 2 failure modes in one continuous 5-month in-service record. CORRECTION 2026-09-21: MetroPT2.csv is a DIFFERENT physical vehicle (train B), not this train's companion -- oil-temp series uncorrelated (r~0), this train's May 30-Jun 2 oil leak invisible in MetroPT2.csv, different healthy bands; hence no post-repair data exists for train A (file ends at export boundary).
